newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Ramsay Healthcare considers float.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Ramsay Healthcare considers float.

text.p: Hospital operator Ramsay Healthcare Ltd said on Tuesday it would decide on a possible float on the Australian Stock Exchange later this month.
"It's an option that's being seriously considered," Ramsay Health Care Planning and Development manager Craig McNally told Reuters.
"If a float was to take place there would be a capital raising," he said.
McNally said he could not say how much capital could be raised or exactly when the Ramsay board would make the decision.
Ramsay operates 13 hospitals and is building two more over the next 12 to 18 months. It employs about 2,500 people.
It has turnover of about A$180 million and this expected to rise by about A$40 million by the year to June 30, 1999.
In the 1995/96 year, Ramsay posted pre-tax and interest earnings of A$20.6 million.
Market sources said Ramsay was considering raising about A$80 million, with an issue of 43 million shares at A$1.85 a share.
This would value the company at up to A$250 million, the sources said.
